subject: Money
title: Mississippi Bubble
description: A micro-lesson that makes Mississippi Bubble usable.

hook.text: In 1720, shares in the Mississippi Company rose 2,000% in months. France's entire economy was a casino.

buildup.text: John Law convinced France to back paper money with shares in his Mississippi Company, which claimed vast riches.

discovery.text: Law created the world's first central bank-like system. Paper money replaced gold. Shares replaced bonds.

twist.text: The riches were imaginary. When investors demanded gold for their shares, there wasn't enough. Panic erupted.

climax.text: France's monetary system collapsed. The word 'bank' became taboo in French for decades.

punchline.text: One man built a financial system. It lasted two years.

quiz.question: What caused the Mississippi Bubble to collapse?
options: The claimed colonial riches were imaginary
